messages:
miguel: thinking out loud — we need a more predictable way to push cheaper variant traffic for lower tiers without blowing latency SLOs. current fallback is too binary and the console UX is confusing for PMs. ideas?
jen: +1. ops asked for percent-based rollout and per-customer opt-out. also need telemetry to show cost delta, otherwise finance will scream.
samir: agree on percent rollout. can we do a policy like: if customer_tier == 'starter' AND avg_latency_ms < 250 then route N% to cheaper_variant?
rachel: that makes sense. we should also consider region constraints — some quantized builds are only in eu-west and us-east for now. routing policy needs region-aware eligibility.
miguel: yes. here's a strawman config snippet for the routing policy we discussed:```
route_policy: {
  name: "tiered_cost_optim",
  conditions: [
    { key: "customer.tier", op: "in", value: ["starter","growth"] },
    { key: "region", op: "in", value: ["us-east","eu-west"] },
    { key: "model.latency_p50_ms", op: "<", value: 250 }
  ],
  variants: [
    { id: "base-v1", weight: 70 },
    { id: "quant-8bit-v1", weight: 30, tag: "cheap" }
  ],
  guardrails: { max_extra_cost_pct: 0, rollback_on_error: true }
}
```
jen: nice. we should expose `variants` weights in the console as a slider + a simple toggle to bind to a percentage-based rollout. UX should show estimated monthly savings and a confidence band.
samir: technically we need to ensure prefix/KV cache compatibility between variants — otherwise switching per-request will cache-miss and spike cost/latency. maybe require cache_compatible: true on variants or add a sticky routing mode (session-based).
miguel: good catch. add `cache_compatible` and `sticky_session` options to the policy. default to sticky for streaming/chat routes.
rachel: telemetry-wise, we need these metrics for each policy: routed_count_by_variant, p50/p95 by variant, tokens_by_variant, cost_estimate_by_variant, and rollback_rate. show per-customer and aggregate.
jen: also add a small sampled eval of output quality (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or model-specific eval set) for starters to detect regressions. not full eval every request — sampled.
miguel: agree. sampling 0.5% of starter traffic and running evals asynchronously. if quality_regression > threshold then auto-deprioritize cheap variant and open a ticket.
samir: implementation questions — do we do routing at edge (API gateway) or at the control plane? edge gives lower hop-count but harder to change weights quickly. control plane can orchestrate but adds hop.
miguel: prefer edge-enforced decision with policy downloaded from control plane. fast path stays in edge runtime. policy updates pushed with versioning and canary.
rachel: console rollout UX: show current policy, history of changes, cost delta, and a single-button rollback. also show per-region variant availability map.
jen: ownership: eng-platform implements policy engine + console hooks, eng-runtime ensures low-overhead evaluation and cache compatibility, eng-ml provides quality eval sampler and variant compatibility matrix.
samir: plan for rollout: 1) feature flag behind org-level opt-in 2) telemetry enabled by default 3) 2-week dogfooding with internal orgs 4) slow external rollout to 'starter' tier first
miguel: sounds good. action items: jen — prototype console slider + savings calc. samir — add cache_compatible flag and sticky routing in runtime. rachel — define telemetry schema and dashboard widgets. i'll draft design doc and RBAC notes for per-customer opt-out.
jen: assigned. will mock a small dashboard in Figma by EOD Friday.
samir: i'll spike the runtime changes next sprint.
rachel: i'll stub the Grafana/console panels and sample events for the infra team.
miguel: thanks. deploy-bot: created task RFC-PLT-172 in backlog for tracking :white_check_mark:
